name: Kung och Adel
description: Kung och Adel (Swedish for 'King and Nobility') is a social card game of the 'President' or 'Asshole' family, flavored with historical Swedish social estates. Players compete to shed their cards and climb the social ladder from Bonden (The Peasant) to Kunegen (The King). The top-ranked players receive bonuses in the form of the best cards from the lower-ranked players in subsequent rounds.

history.origins: Derived from the ancient 'Warlords' or 'Dai Hin Min' families of games, it was adapted in the late 19th/early 20th century to reflect the Swedish Estate system (StÃ¥ndsriksdagen).
timeline: 1900s: Hierarchy games gain popularity in Swedish schools.
1970s: The name 'Kung och Adel' becomes standardized as a variant of 'Skitgubbe' style social hierarchy.
Present: A very common household and party game in Sweden.
history.cultural: Used as a humorous metaphor for social mobility and class struggle in Swedish student circles.
history.evolution: The game evolved to include specific 'Feudal taxes' where the King can demand specific cards from the Peasant, ensuring a cycle of power.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. 2s are usually 'clearing' cards or wildcards.
setup.dealing: The whole deck is dealt out evenly among players.

rules.objective: Be the first to shed all cards to become the King for the next round.
rules.gameplay:
1. Standard shedding logic: Play a card (or set of equal cards) higher than the current top card.
2. **The Tax (Skatt)**: Before play, the Peasant must give their two best cards (Aces/2s) to the King. The King gives back their two worst cards (low numerals). The Nobility and Burghers exchange one card similarly.
keyRules: 10s may also clear the pile in some variants
Tax exchange: Peasant gives 2 best to King, gets 2 worst back
Social ranks determine seating and card exchanges

strategy.basic: As the King, use your 'Taxes' (the high cards from the Peasant) to control the game immediately. Lead with a pair of High cards to prevent anyone else from taking control early.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Peasant Revolution': If you are the Peasant, and you have a 2 (Burner), don't give it up in the tax if you can help it. Use it mid-round to break the King's control and jump to the 'Nobility' rank.
strategy.advanced: Stalling: If you are the King, 'pass' your turn even if you can play, if you think someone else can clear the pile with a card you want to save for later. This 'baits' the Nobility into using their high cards.
tips: Always know who is next to finish. If the person to your left is the Burgher, they are your biggest threat to promotion.
Keep a 2 (or a 10) for your very last card. It's the most reliable way to clear your hand and ensure you finish first.
